proposals.after: In year three he received appointment as Linhuang Prefecture judge and provisional right deputy army supervisor under the marshal.
proposals.reason: 推官 is a prefectural judicial office (judge), not an investigating censor (御史).

proposals.before: In the third year he was appointed investigating censor of Linhuang Prefecture and acted as right deputy army supervisor under the marshal.
proposals.after: In the third year he was appointed judge of Linhuang Prefecture and acted as right deputy army supervisor under the marshal.
proposals.reason: 推官 is a prefectural judicial office (judge), not an investigating censor (御史).

proposals.before: Before long, plotting to escape and return to Jin territory, he sent Fengxian magistrate Heshenlie Bulige, Bejing instructor Pucha Hulian, and Right Three Departments inspector Pucha Punü across the sea to bring word.
proposals.after: Before long, plotting to escape and return to Jin territory, he sent Fengxian magistrate Heshenlie Bulige, Beijing instructor Pucha Hulian, and Right Three Departments inspector Pucha Punü across the sea to bring word.

proposals.before: Before long, planning to break free and return to the Jin, he sent Fengxian magistrate Heshenlie Bulige, Bejing instructor Pucha Hulian, and Right Three Departments inspector Pucha Punü across the sea to report.
proposals.after: Before long, planning to break free and return to the Jin, he sent Fengxian magistrate Heshenlie Bulige, Beijing instructor Pucha Hulian, and Right Three Departments inspector Pucha Punü across the sea to report.

proposals.after: In the tenth month the Tangut forces attacked Suide Prefecture and encamped on Zhutian Mountain.
proposals.reason: 綏德州 is Suide Prefecture, not Sui Prefecture.

proposals.before: In the tenth month the Xia people attacked Sui Prefecture and encamped on Zhutian Mountain.
proposals.after: In the tenth month the Xia people attacked Suide Prefecture and encamped on Zhutian Mountain.
proposals.reason: 綏德州 is Suide Prefecture, not Sui Prefecture.

proposals.before: On the first gengyin day of the seventh month of year 7 he was removed from the chief councilor post and made vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
proposals.after: On the gengyin first day of the seventh month of year 7 he was removed from the chief councilor post and made vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
proposals.reason: 庚寅朔 means the first day of the month, which was a gengyin day, not the first of several gengyin days.

proposals.before: On the first jiwei day of the tenth month an edict ordered Heda and vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Pu'a to relieve Weizhou.
proposals.after: On the jiwei first day of the tenth month an edict ordered Heda and vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Pu'a to relieve Weizhou.

proposals.before: Before long Pu'a was made acting participant in the administration of the Secretariat and together with Heda conducted branch secretariat affairs at Wenxiang to prepare for Tong Pass.
proposals.after: Before long Pu'a was made acting participant in determining Secretariat affairs and together with Heda conducted branch secretariat affairs at Wenxiang to prepare for Tong Pass.
proposals.reason: Chinese 參和政事 is the office 參知政事; 和 is a graphic error for 知, and 'administration of the Secretariat' hides that office.

proposals.before: Biography: Yi Lapua
proposals.after: Yila Pu'a
proposals.reason: 移剌 is the surname Yila and 蒲阿 the given name; the fused English Yi Lapua splits the name wrongly, and Biography is not in the Chinese heading.

proposals.before: A Khitan by origin, he entered military service young and through merit rose from wanhu to army marshal.
proposals.after: A Khitan by origin, he entered military service young and through merit rose from qianhu (commander of a thousand) to army marshal.
proposals.reason: 千戶 is a commander of a thousand (qianhu), not wanhu (萬戶, commander of ten thousand).

proposals.before: He was originally a Khitan; from youth he followed the army, and through merit was promoted from wanhu to army marshal.
proposals.after: He was originally a Khitan; from youth he followed the army, and through merit was promoted from qianhu (commander of a thousand) to army marshal.
proposals.reason: Same 千戶/wanhu mismatch in the literal rendering.

proposals.before: In winter, in the twelfth month of the second year of Yuanguang, on gengyin, Emperor Xuanzong fell gravely ill. The crown prince's elder half-brother Prince Ying Shouchun entered first to attend him; the crown prince knocked at the Eastern Palace gate seeking audience and ordered Pu'a to don armor beneath his robe, gather troops, and encamp at Genyue against any emergency.
proposals.after: In winter, in the twelfth month of the second year of Yuanguang, on gengyin, Emperor Xuanzong fell gravely ill. The crown prince's elder half-brother Prince Ying Shouchun entered first to attend him; the crown prince came from the Eastern Palace, knocked at the gate seeking audience, and ordered Pu'a to don armor beneath his robe, gather troops, and encamp at Genyue against any emergency.
proposals.reason: 太子自東宮扣門 is the crown prince going from the Eastern Palace and knocking for audience, not knocking at the Eastern Palace gate.

proposals.before: In winter, in the twelfth month of the second year of Yuanguang, on gengyin, Emperor Xuanzong's illness grew grave; the crown prince's elder half-brother Prince Ying Shouchun entered first to attend the illness; the crown prince knocked at the Eastern Palace gate seeking audience; he ordered Pu'a to don armor beneath his robe, gather troops, and encamp at Genyue against the unexpected.
proposals.after: In winter, in the twelfth month of the second year of Yuanguang, on gengyin, Emperor Xuanzong's illness grew grave; the crown prince's elder half-brother Prince Ying Shouchun entered first to attend the illness; the crown prince from the Eastern Palace knocked at the gate seeking audience; he ordered Pu'a to don armor beneath his robe, gather troops, and encamp at Genyue against the unexpected.
proposals.reason: Same reversed locative: 自東宮 marks origin, not the gate being knocked.

proposals.before: After this Chief Councilor Sai Bu was sent to handle Secretariat affairs in Guanzhong, Chief Councilor Heda was recalled to court, Ba Sa was summoned to the palace, and Pu'a led Wanyan Chen Heshang with one thousand Zhongxiao Army troops to garrison Bin Prefecture and observe northern movements.
proposals.after: After this Chief Councilor Sai Bu was sent to handle Secretariat affairs in Guanzhong, Manager of Governmental Affairs Heda was recalled to court, Ba Sa was summoned to the palace, and Pu'a led Wanyan Chen Heshang with one thousand Zhongxiao Army troops to garrison Bin Prefecture and observe northern movements.
proposals.reason: 平章政事合達 is not 丞相; only Sai Bu is called 丞相 in this sentence.

proposals.before: Heda then asked Andemu, and Mu thought otherwise.
proposals.after: Heda then asked Andemu, and Andemu thought otherwise.
proposals.reason: 木 is the same person as 按得木, not a second referent named Mu.

proposals.before: On the jiaxu day, before sunrise, the northern army arrived; the great commander came forward under two small guide flags to reconnoiter, then did not advance but spread out like geese in flight, swung along the mountain foot to emerge behind the Jin cavalry, and advanced in three columns—aside from baggage trains, more than twenty thousand men remained.
proposals.after: On the jiaxu day, before sunrise, the northern army arrived; the great commander came forward under two small guide flags to reconnoiter, then did not advance but spread out like geese in flight, swung along the mountain foot to emerge behind the cavalry, and advanced in three columns—aside from baggage trains, more than twenty thousand men remained.
proposals.reason: Chinese 騎兵 is unmarked cavalry; the idiomatic rendering invents 'Jin' before cavalry.

proposals.before: The court would not accept this.
proposals.after: They did not follow this.
proposals.reason: 不從 refers to the commanders not adopting Pu'a's counsel, not a decision by the court.

proposals.before: On the guimao day the great army set out from Deng Prefecture for the capital: twenty thousand cavalry and one hundred thirty thousand infantry; cavalry under Pucha Dingzhu, Pucha Dajibu, and commandant Andemu; Zhongxiao Army under overall leaders Jiagu Aida and imperial clansman Daluhuan; overall leader Jiagu Yitelie; infantry under army controller Linzi Prince Zhang Hui; extermination bandit commandants Wanyan Apai, Gao Ying, and Fan Ze; center army under Chen Heshang—joined with Duke of Hengshan Wuxian and Yang Woyan's forces.
proposals.after: On the guiwei day the great army set out from Deng Prefecture for the capital: twenty thousand cavalry and one hundred thirty thousand infantry; cavalry under Pucha Dingzhu, Pucha Dajibu, and commandant Andemu; Zhongxiao Army under overall leaders Jiagu Aida and imperial clansman Daluhuan; overall leader Jiagu Yitelie; infantry under army controller Linzi Prince Zhang Hui; extermination bandit commandants Wanyan Apai, Gao Ying, and Fan Ze; center army under Chen Heshang—joined with Duke of Hengshan Wuxian and Yang Woyan's forces.
proposals.reason: Chinese 癸未 is guiwei, not guimao (癸卯).

proposals.before: On the guimao day the great army set out from Deng Prefecture toward the capital: twenty thousand cavalry, one hundred thirty thousand infantry; cavalry commanders Pucha Dingzhu, Pucha Dajibu, and commandant Andemu; Zhongxiao Army overall leaders Jiagu Aida and imperial clansman Daluhuan; overall leader Jiagu Yitelie; infantry army controller Linzi Prince Zhang Hui; extermination bandit commandants Wanyan Apai, Gao Ying, and Fan Ze; center army Chen Heshang—joined with Duke of Hengshan Wuxian and Yang Woyan's armies.
proposals.after: On the guiwei day the great army set out from Deng Prefecture toward the capital: twenty thousand cavalry, one hundred thirty thousand infantry; cavalry commanders Pucha Dingzhu, Pucha Dajibu, and commandant Andemu; Zhongxiao Army overall leaders Jiagu Aida and imperial clansman Daluhuan; overall leader Jiagu Yitelie; infantry army controller Linzi Prince Zhang Hui; extermination bandit commandants Wanyan Apai, Gao Ying, and Fan Ze; center army Chen Heshang—joined with Duke of Hengshan Wuxian and Yang Woyan's armies.
proposals.reason: Chinese 癸未 is guiwei, not guimao (癸卯).

proposals.before: Wuxian led thirty horsemen into the bamboo grove; the armies of Yang, Fan, and Zhang fought over the road as the northern army surrounded them in layer after layer; together with Gao Ying's remnant troops they fought south of Shilin Village; Woyan, Fan, and Ying all fell; only Zhang Hui, on foot with a great spear in hand, fought to the death.
proposals.after: Wuxian led thirty horsemen into the bamboo grove; the armies of Yang, Fan, and Zhang fought over the road as the northern army surrounded them in layer after layer; together with Gao Ying's remnant troops they fought south of Shilin Village; Woyan, Ze, and Ying all fell; only Zhang Hui, on foot with a great spear in hand, fought to the death.
proposals.reason: 澤 is the given name parallel to 沃衍 and 英 (Yang Woyan, Fan Ze, Gao Ying); rendering it as surname Fan in the death clause reverses the naming pattern used for the other two.

proposals.before: Wuxian led thirty cavalry into the bamboo grove; the armies of Yang, Fan, and Zhang fought over the road; the northern army surrounded them in several rings; together with Gao Ying's remnant troops they fought south of Shilin Village; Woyan, Fan, and Ying all died; only Zhang Hui on foot wielding a great spear fought hard and perished.
proposals.after: Wuxian led thirty cavalry into the bamboo grove; the armies of Yang, Fan, and Zhang fought over the road; the northern army surrounded them in several rings; together with Gao Ying's remnant troops they fought south of Shilin Village; Woyan, Ze, and Ying all died; only Zhang Hui on foot wielding a great spear fought hard and perished.
proposals.reason: 澤 should be transliterated Ze as a given name, matching 沃衍/Woyan and 英/Ying; Fan is the surname used earlier for the army, not the given name in 沃衍、澤、英.

decisions.reason: 授臨潢府推官 names the prefectural judicial office 推官, not an investigating censor (御史).
The same 臨潢府推官 is a prefectural judgeship; the literal “investigating censor” is unsupported.
北京教授 is Beijing instructor; “Bejing” is a misspelling of the place name.
The literal likewise misspells 北京 as Bejing; Beijing is the supported reading.
夏人攻綏德州 names Suide Prefecture; “Sui Prefecture” drops 德.
The literal “Sui Prefecture” likewise omits 德 from 綏德州.

decisions.after: On the first day of the seventh month of year 7, a gengyin day, he was removed from the chief councilor post and made vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
decisions.reason: 庚寅朔 is the first day of the month, which was a gengyin day. The original “first gengyin day” can be read as the first of several gengyin days; the proposed “gengyin first day” is an awkward calque.

decisions.after: On the first day of the tenth month, a jiwei day, an edict ordered Heda and vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Pu'a to relieve Weizhou.
decisions.reason: 己未朔 is the first day of the month, which was a jiwei day. The original “first jiwei day” is ambiguous, and the proposed “jiwei first day” is awkward.

decisions.after: Before long Pu'a was made acting participant in determining governmental matters and together with Heda conducted branch secretariat affairs at Wenxiang to prepare for Tong Pass.
decisions.reason: The chapter’s 權參和政事 is a graphic slip for the office 參知政事 (Wikisource’s parallel in the same juan: 以權參知政事與合達行省於閿鄉). The original “administration of the Secretariat” hides that office; “determining Secretariat affairs” is still off, because 政事 are governmental matters.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 未幾，以權參知政事與合達行省於閿鄉

decisions.reason: The heading is only 移剌蒲阿, surname Yila plus given name Pu'a; “Biography:” is not in the Chinese, and Yi Lapua splits the name wrongly.
以勞自千戶遷都統 starts from a commander of a thousand (千戶), not a wanhu (萬戶).
The literal likewise renders 千戶 as wanhu; qianhu is the supported rank.
太子自東宮扣門求見 marks the Eastern Palace as the crown prince’s point of departure; he knocks for audience, not at the Eastern Palace gate.
The same 自東宮 is origin, not the gate being struck; the revised locative is accurate.
Only 丞相賽不 is Chief Councilor; 召平章政事合達還朝 recalls Heda as Manager of Governmental Affairs, a distinct office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以丞相賽不行尚書省事於關中，召平章政事合達還朝

decisions.reason: 合達乃問按得木，木以為不然 abbreviates 按得木 as 木; expanding to Andemu avoids inventing a second person named Mu. The source-based short name 木 remains valid as an alias.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 合達乃問按得木，木以為不然

decisions.reason: 出騎兵之後 refers to the cavalry just posted 山后 in s0155, i.e. the Jin deployment. Adding “Jin” is a contextual gloss, not a false invention; dropping it is merely more literal.
不從 has no court as subject; after Pu'a’s field counsel it means the commanders did not follow that advice.
癸未 follows 壬午朔 and is guiwei, not guimao (癸卯).
The literal likewise misreads 癸未 as guimao; guiwei is the sexagenary day in the Chinese.
沃衍、澤、英皆死 lists given names parallel to Woyan and Ying; 澤 is Ze, not the surname Fan used earlier for 樊軍.
The literal death clause should likewise render 澤 as Ze, matching 沃衍 and 英.

claimRevisions.reason: The accepted heading repair restores the English personal name to Yila Pu'a; Yi Lapua was produced only by the fused mistranslation.
